title: the control plane Data Layer record
description: Machine-validatable Data Layer (docs/spec/foundations/layering-and-versioning.md; DCM ADR-012). A request payload is assembled by merging ordered layers lowest-authority-first; every field a layer sets records that layer's uuid as its provenance source. UDLM carries the layer records; the control plane's assembly engine merges them. Layers carry DATA (the what); Policies (policy.schema.json) decide/transform (the how). data-model-core.md §2 [D8.4].

uuid.description: RFC 9562 v4 identity. This uuid is the field-provenance source recorded for every field this layer sets (layering-and-versioning §provenance).

supersedes.description: LINEAGE — the single, explicit mechanism (UDLM ADR-012; the decision-record 'never edit, supersede' idiom; layers are the reference member of ADR-051's immutable-record family). A layer version is IMMUTABLE: any change is a NEW record (its own identity uuid + a higher version), never an edit of the old one, and this array names the uuid(s) of the version(s) it directly supersedes. Absent = a lineage ROOT (a first version, or a genuinely new entity). Because it is a uuid array it expresses ANY lineage shape — linear (supersedes the one prior), fork (two records each supersede the same prior), merge (one record supersedes several), rename (supersede a prior at a different handle). It is authoritative (uuid-based); `handle` is advisory display only and is NOT a lineage signal. Each uuid MUST resolve to an existing layer of the same reference_data_type with a strictly lower version (validate.py check_layer_lineage). Change-impact is derived from this DAG plus the reverse reference index — which records reference a version that has since been superseded.

tenant_uuid.description: Owning tenant (TEN-001). system/platform-domain layers (base, core, reference_data) are owned by the platform tenant; tenant-domain layers by the consuming tenant.

layer_type.description:
The layer types (layering-and-versioning §3). Six are ASSEMBLY positions, ordered by authority: base (foundation, every chain begins here), core (standards/compliance defaults), intermediate (org/customization — a business unit, an enclave, an application team's configuration set), service (catalog/provider), request (the consumer's direct declaration — highest data authority), policy (applied over the merged result).

`reference_data` is the seventh and is NOT an assembly position: it marks a layer that OTHER LAYERS REFERENCE — shared data, defined once and pointed at by `data_reference` rather than merged by precedence. Ruled 2026-08-11 to stay, correcting ADR-054's draft retirement. Two kinds of record were misfiled under it and have moved: a governed vocabulary TERM (matched against, never merged — now `vocabulary-term.schema.json`) and an application-team config set (contributed, so an `intermediate` layer). The test is what the record does — matched, contributed, or pointed at.

reference_data_type.description: REQUIRED when layer_type is reference_data (enforced below): the kind of shared dataset this layer governs — e.g. location, os_image, vm_size, network_zone, network_tier, storage_class, gpu_profile, environment, topology_capability (layering-and-versioning §3.7). A data reference (a URF string `uuid/<v4>[@version][?reference_data_type==<kind>]`; UDLM ADR-012) is only valid against a reference_data layer of the SAME reference_data_type — the type is the match axis the reference declares. Meaningless on non-reference_data layers.

covers.description: TARGET scoping (publish side; ADR-054 two-sided scoping): ONE URF filter (identifier-scheme §9) naming which resources this layer MAY inject into — e.g. estate?resource_type==Compute.* or estate?labels.concern==payments. The assembly engine GATHERS every layer whose covers matches the target, then orders by precedence; covers says *who may*, the request's from_layers says *who does*. OPTIONAL — do not duplicate resource_type: a type-scoped layer (resource_type: X) already targets X (≡ covers "estate?resource_type==X.*"), so its covers is DERIVED and omitted. When both are set, covers MUST match the layer's own resource_type (validate.py check_layer). covers is Data (the declaration); the match is Policy (the assembly engine).

applies_on.description: TARGET scoping (publish side; ADR-054). The convergence scenario(s) this layer injects during — named by ADR-030's colloquial vocabulary (realize · reconcile · reconfigure · rehydrate · decommission; migration is a realize/rehydrate onto a new provider). These are trigger/gap-shape shortcuts for the one Converge act (ADR-030), not distinct mechanisms, so the value is an open lowercase token set rather than a closed enum. Absent = injects on every scenario. Injection requires the request's convergence operation ∈ this list.

from_layers.description: SOURCE scoping (subscribe side; ADR-054): ONE URF filter selecting which layers feed THIS request. OPTIONAL OVERRIDE — tenant isolation is the DEFAULT, not a re-declaration: absent, assembly draws the request's own tenant's layers plus platform/system-domain layers, never another tenant's. Declare only to select an EXPLICIT subset. Injection = the intersection: L injects into R iff R.target matches L.covers (or L.resource_type) ∧ R.operation ∈ L.applies_on ∧ L matches R.from_layers (default: tenant+platform) ∧ L not matched by R.skip. Injection is an ingress crossing — PROJ-006 admission applies (ADR-041).

skip.description: SOURCE scoping (subscribe side; ADR-054): the negative form — ONE URF filter naming layers to EXCLUDE even though their covers matches. Governed: freely skippable for defaults, but narrow_only/compliance layers require authorization to skip (control-plane policy step).

precedence_class.description: Position in the assembly precedence chain, lowest-authority first: base → core → intermediate → service → request, with policy applied over the result. Higher classes override lower field-by-field (narrow-never-widen for constraint profiles, E1). Usually equals layer_type; reference_data layers are looked up, not merged, so they declare their functional class.

precedence_order.description: Optional fine-grained ordering WITHIN a precedence_class (e.g. multiple stacked intermediate layers); higher wins. Ties break by class then by declared chain order.

domain.description: Ownership/precedence scope. resource_type-scoped layers MUST declare resource_type.

resource_type.description: When the layer is type-scoped: the Category.Type it applies to. A type-scoped base layer must conform to that type's universal field requirements (layering-and-versioning §3.1).

contributor.description: Who may author this layer + the review it requires (layering-and-versioning §2; federated-contribution-model §3).

review.description: request layers = none (direct consumer declaration); all others flow through the GitOps PR review model.

fields.description: The DATA this layer contributes to the assembled payload — dot-path-or-nested field values. Each field set here records THIS layer's uuid as its provenance source. Values are typed by the target Resource Type Spec and are not re-validated here (the layer is a partial contribution, not a complete entity).

extends.description:
The layer(s) this one extends — explicit lineage, readable from the record instead of reconstructible only by running assembly. Any layer may be a parent and any layer a child: the reference is what creates the relationship, so no layer needs marking as extensible — being pointed at is a property of the pointer, not the target, which is how the class system already works.

A LIST, because a template or composite request draws on several lineages at once, and each extension carries its OWN matching criteria — `when` — so which parents apply depends on the context being assembled.

VALUES OVERRIDE, LIMITS INTERSECT, and the asymmetry is what makes multiple parents safe. If `limits` merged like values, a permissive parent would erase a restrictive one's bound and you could buy permission by extending one more thing. Intersecting is MONOTONE: another parent can only tighten. A bound has no override; `skip` is the route, and it declines the layer's participation visibly.

A CYCLE IS REFUSED: an extension chain that loops computes no value, and the model refuses what cannot be computed. DEPTH IS NOT CAPPED — deep chains are normal here, and how deep is too deep is a policy judgement, never a structural one.

layer.description: The parent, as a URF reference — authored by handle, resolved to the uuid form (WIR-004). It resolves to a layer record; nothing else about that layer has to opt in.

when.description: OPTIONAL — the criteria under which THIS extension applies. Same equality-only grammar as a constraint clause, for the same reason: it has to stay decidable. Absent, the extension always applies.

reason.description: OPTIONAL — why this lineage is drawn on. For the human reading a deep chain; never evaluated.

limits.description:
The envelope this layer's DESCENDANTS must stay inside — keyed by dot-path into the fields it bounds, each holding a list of constraint clauses whose union is the permitted set.

ABSENT MEANS UNBOUNDED, NEVER EMPTY. A layer that says nothing constrains nothing (NDF-001 — UDLM ships no defaults). The expected shape is wide or silent at the base, tightening as each extension determines the use case further — the same convergence the class tier runs when a declared range collapses to a selected value.

AN ENVELOPE RATHER THAN A DIRECTION FLAG. A layer could instead declare only 'tighten, never loosen'; that is weaker because a direction can be judged solely against whatever happened to merge beneath it, so the legality of a layer cannot be established without assembling everything under it first. A declared envelope is checkable against every descendant independently, which is what makes one validation pass work over a deep chain.

WHO ENFORCES IT IS NOT UDLM. A Class's `supports` containment is a gate, because a Class is UDLM's own portable artifact. A layer holds an estate's configuration, so what is permitted there is the estate's call: the envelope is DATA here and a policy enforces it (`policy_type: validation`) — one generic policy reading declared limits, not one policy per case.

additionalProperties.description: The clauses bounding this field. Union of those whose `when` holds; a descendant's own clauses must be CONTAINED in the intersection of every applicable ancestor envelope.

narrow_only.description: When true, this is a constraint/narrowing layer (E1): it may only TIGHTEN field markers/values declared by lower layers, never loosen them (narrow-never-widen). Recorded so the assembly engine enforces the direction.
